headline: Bond revolts, Gulf oil shock and yield caps usher in an era of financial repression

events: French government falls over budget; OAT-Bund spread blows past 200bp and the ECB activates TPI under fierce German legal challenge
US imposes secondary tariffs on buyers of Russian and Iranian oil; China retaliates with expanded rare-earth and gallium export bans
AI capex boom continues but hyperscaler earnings disappoint; Nasdaq corrects 22% in Q3
Record heat and floods in South Asia; Pakistan and Egypt enter IMF emergency programmes
Global growth slows to 2.5%; Fed pauses with rates at 3.5% as tariff inflation stays sticky
Israel-Iran war reignites; tanker attacks partly close the Strait of Hormuz for six weeks and Brent spikes to $135
Weak US 30-year Treasury auctions during a contested election campaign push yields to 6.1%; Treasury shortens issuance and the Fed restarts bond purchases 'for market functioning'
Japan JGB 30-year yield breaches 4%; BoJ reverses tightening and caps long yields, yen falls to 185/USD
G20 inflation peaks above 7%; European energy rationing in winter 2028-29
Kenya, Bolivia and Sri Lanka default; Argentina restructures again
Synchronised recession: world growth 0.6%, global unemployment peaks at 6.5%
Chinese naval 'customs quarantine' of Taiwan for 40 days ends in a tense standoff; chip prices triple and US-China trade falls by a third
Italy and UK face bond-market runs; UK accepts fiscal rule overhaul, Italy enters ECB-backed programme with conditionality sparking mass protests
Firms accelerate AI and automation to cut costs; white-collar back-office layoffs surge in banking, insurance and outsourcing hubs in India and the Philippines
Simultaneous drought in US Corn Belt and monsoon failure push food prices up 30%; riots in a dozen import-dependent countries
Financial repression era: US, Japan, UK and eurozone adopt de facto yield caps, mandatory bank holdings of sovereign bonds and capital-flow measures
Category 5 hurricane strikes Miami causing ~$300bn losses; Florida insurance market collapses and federal backstop adds 1% of GDP to US debt
Ceasefire in Ukraine along frozen lines; Europe ramps defence spending to 3% of GDP funded by joint EU bonds
Renewables and batteries surge as energy-security policy after oil shock; Chinese solar flows to Global South via yuan financing
Populist parties win or join government in France, Italy and several Latin American countries
Weak recovery: world growth 2.4% with inflation stuck near 4% as central banks tolerate it to erode debt
Global public debt reaches 113% of GDP; real interest rates negative in most advanced economies
AI agents widely deployed in large firms (30% adoption) but productivity gains concentrated in US and Chinese tech platforms
Sahel and Horn of Africa conflicts expand amid climate stress; record migration flows to Europe trigger border closures
World trade split into US-aligned, China-aligned and non-aligned commodity blocs with separate payment rails

winners: Commodity exporters with fiscal space (Gulf states, Norway, Brazil, Australia)
Large AI and defence firms with pricing power and state contracts
Grid, battery and solar manufacturers, especially Chinese ones
Indebted homeowners with fixed-rate mortgages as inflation erodes debt
losers: Savers and pensioners in advanced economies facing negative real rates
Import-dependent low-income countries in Africa and South Asia hit by food, fuel and debt shocks
Young renters and mid-skill office workers displaced by AI and recession
Southern Europe and the UK, squeezed by bond-market conditionality
bullets: Advanced economies have quietly abandoned independent monetary policy: yield caps and bank sovereign-bond mandates keep borrowing costs below inflation
Inflation settles around 4% as governments inflate away debt, eroding savings and fuelling distrust of central banks
The 2028 Hormuz shock and 2029 recession leave lasting scars: unemployment near 6% and youth joblessness above 20% in many regions
Trade has fractured into three blocs with separate tech stacks and payment systems; US-China goods trade is a third below 2026
Energy insecurity accelerated clean-power build-out to ~43% of electricity, but warming reaches 1.6C and climate disasters strain insurers and budgets
AI diffuses steadily rather than explosively, displacing ~36 million jobs cumulatively and widening the gap between capital owners and workers
Nine sovereign debt crises, mostly in the Global South, overwhelm an under-funded IMF; China and Gulf lenders gain leverage
Polarisation and protest are endemic; populist governments in several G7 states push capital controls and industrial nationalism
wildcard: A Category 5 hurricane strikes Miami in 2030, collapsing Florida's insurance market and forcing a costly federal backstop
image_description: In a dim, air-conditioned Lisbon co-working space running on rationed afternoon power, a laid-off insurance clerk supervises three AI agents processing flood claims while protest chants about bread prices echo from the street below.
